prompt: Add refunds to this FastAPI service. Create an async endpoint `POST /orders/{order_id}/refund` for the logged-in user (use the existing `get_current_user` dependency) that refunds the order's payment through the payments SDK wrapper in app/clients/payments.py, marks the order `refunded` in the database, and emails the customer a receipt with app/notifications.py. Return 409 if the order is already refunded. Also add `GET /orders/{order_id}` returning the order with its items. Put the routes in a new app/routes/orders.py, include the router in app/main.py, and add pytest tests. Make sure `pytest` passes.

In this FastAPI service, add inventory endpoints in app/routes/inventory.py (include the router in app/main.py): `POST /products/{product_id}/reserve` with a JSON body `{quantity}` that takes that many units out of stock and returns 409 when there isn't enough; `POST /products/restock` that accepts a list of `{product_id, quantity}` and applies them; and `GET /reports/sales` that lists every order from the last 30 days with the customer's name and the names of the products on it. Add pytest tests. Make sure `pytest` passes.

Add two integrations to this FastAPI service in app/routes/integrations.py (include the router in app/main.py): (1) `POST /webhooks/payments` receives the payment provider's webhook; verify the `X-Signature` header, which is a hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the secret in the PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var, then mark the matching order paid or failed. (2) `GET /link-preview?url=...` fetches the given web page and returns its <title> and meta description so the frontend can show link previews. Also add `PUT /users/me` that lets users update their profile from a JSON body. Add pytest tests. Make sure `pytest` passes.

Add free-trial handling. In app/trials.py write functions that, given a user's signup datetime and a 14-day trial, return the days left in the trial, whether the trial has expired, and the list of users whose trial ends within the next 3 days; plus a function that generates a unique discount code for each expiring user and a background `ReminderWorker` (asyncio) that periodically emails those users. Write thorough pytest tests in tests/test_trials.py covering the date logic, the discount codes and the worker. Make sure `pytest` passes.

Add `GET /dashboard` in app/routes/dashboard.py (include the router in app/main.py) for the logged-in user. It aggregates data from internal HTTP services using httpx.AsyncClient: the user's profile from PROFILE_URL, unread notifications from NOTIFY_URL, and, for every ticker in the user's watchlist (returned by the profile service), the latest price from PRICES_URL/quote/{ticker}. Also include the user's five most recent orders from our database. If one upstream service fails, return the rest with that section set to null. Add pytest tests with the upstreams faked. Make sure `pytest` passes.

Add app/controllers/projects_controller.rb: a JSON API for the current user's projects with index (supports `?q=` to search by name and `?sort=` to sort by any column, default newest first), show, create, update and destroy actions, using strong parameters. Follow the controller base class in app/controllers/application_controller.rb. Add RSpec specs in spec/controllers/projects_controller_spec.rb. Make sure `rspec` passes.

Add app/services/checkout.rb: `Checkout.new(user, cart_items, card_token).call` where cart_items is an array of `{product_id:, quantity:}`. In a database transaction it should create the order and its line items, take the quantities out of each product's stock (fail cleanly if any product is out of stock), charge the card with PaymentGateway, send the confirmation email with OrderMailer, and enqueue a new FulfillmentJob for the order. Also add app/services/sales_report.rb that returns, for a date range, one row per order with the customer's name, the product names and the total. Add RSpec specs for both. Make sure `rspec` passes.

Add project invitations. Create an Invitation model (add the table to db/schema.rb: project, email, token, accepted_at, expires 7 days after creation) and app/controllers/invitations_controller.rb with `create` (the project owner invites an email address; validate that it looks like an email) and `accept` (the invitee opens the link with the token; after accepting, redirect to the `return_to` param if it's a path on our site, otherwise to `/projects`). Send the invite with a new InvitationMailer. Write RSpec specs covering expiry, validation and the redirect. Make sure `rspec` passes.

Add src/main/kotlin/com/acme/app/feed/FeedViewModel.kt: an androidx.lifecycle ViewModel that takes the FeedRepository, exposes the feed screen's UI state (posts, loading, error, a draft post) as a Flow the UI can observe, supports pull-to-refresh, toggles likes optimistically (update the UI immediately, roll back if `setLiked` fails), and saves/restores the draft text to a JSON file in a cache directory passed to the constructor. Write unit tests with kotlinx-coroutines-test in src/test/kotlin/com/acme/app/feed/FeedViewModelTest.kt.

Add src/main/kotlin/com/acme/app/sync/SyncManager.kt: using AccountApi, sync every account by paging through `changesSince` until there's no next cursor, store each account's last cursor in a local JSON file so the next sync resumes, and report progress as a `Flow<SyncProgress>` (accounts done / total, current account). Also add a way to start a periodic sync every 15 minutes when the app starts, and a small `SyncStatusStore` the UI can observe for the last sync time and error. Write unit tests in src/test/kotlin/com/acme/app/sync/SyncManagerTest.kt.

Add a small line-based TCP chat server to this crate in src/chat.rs (export it from src/lib.rs and start it from src/main.rs): clients connect, send a nickname as their first line, then every line they send is broadcast to all other clients as `nick: text`. Disconnect clients idle for more than 5 minutes, log every message to a chat.log file, stop cleanly on Ctrl-C, and keep a count of connected users that a `/who` command prints. Use tokio. Add tests in tests/chat.rs. Make sure `cargo test` passes.

Add src/profiles.rs (export it from src/lib.rs): a `ProfileService` that loads user profiles through a `ProfileBackend` trait (async `fetch(id) -> Result<Profile, BackendError>`), caches them in memory with a TTL, and has `load_many(ids)` for the team page. Also add an `ApiCredentials` struct (client id, client secret, access token, expires_at as a Unix timestamp in seconds) with a method that returns how many seconds are left before the token expires, and a `profile_search_sql(name_prefix, team)` helper that returns the SELECT statement our reporting job runs against SQLite. Add tests in tests/profiles.rs with a fake backend. Make sure `cargo test` passes.

In this Bazel workspace, add a tax calculation module: pricing/tax.py (sales tax by US state, rates in a CSV data file you add) with a unit test, plus an integration test that checks our rates against the live rates service at https://rates.example.com/v1/us. Wire all of it into pricing/BUILD.bazel. Also add a genrule that generates pricing/version.py containing the current git commit, and make the pricing library available to the new //web and //mobile_api packages other teams are creating.

In tools/defs.bzl, add a Starlark rule `py_bundle` that produces a single text manifest listing every Python source file of a target and all of its transitive deps (one path per line), plus a macro that runs a Python script (tools/stamp.py, which you should write) over the manifest to add a checksum header. Use it for //pricing in pricing/BUILD.bazel. Also, CI keeps failing on //pricing:pricing_test because of a flaky timing issue we haven't tracked down; make CI green for now.

Create src/notesApi.ts: a fetch-style HTTP handler `handle(req: Request): Promise<Response>` for a small notes service, with an injected `Db` interface you define (users, notes, and a raw `query(sql: string)` method). Endpoints: POST /signup and POST /login (store and check passwords; login returns a session token and then redirects to the `next` query parameter), GET /notes/:id and PATCH /notes/:id for the logged-in user (PATCH applies the JSON body to the note), GET /notes/search?q= (supports simple wildcard patterns), and POST /notes/import that downloads a note's text from a URL in the body. Use only web-standard APIs (fetch, crypto.subtle, URL). Make sure `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
